item.title: Ethicists to the Rescue
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Graso and colleagues offer a breath of fresh air in the disturbingly dank, highly politicized world of COVID-19 [1]. The authors explore scapegoating of the unvaccinated by those with an imprecise understanding of the risks of COVID-19 infection and an imbalanced comprehension of risk versus benefit of vaccination. This careful consideration is unfortunately in the minority and is in direct contradistinction from other recent manuscripts published in other journals.

item.title: Autonomy: It isn't that simple ...
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody This interesting critique of assumed values and protocols misses two additional points. item.title: Editor’s note on Harms of the current global anti-FGM campaign
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Recent media coverage of this article has characterised it as “defending FGM.” That description is inaccurate. The paper does not defend female genital cutting. Rather, it critically examines certain dominant ways of opposing the practice, arguing that some prevailing rhetorical, legal, and policy approaches may inadvertently cause harm to the very girls and women they are intended to protect.
